sentences.text:
Hon'Ble Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.737 of 2019
Judgment:

1. Dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-The Court of Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad, passed in M.V.O.P.No.1397 of 2012, dated 09.04.2014, the petitioner/injured preferred the present Appeal seeking for enhancement of the same.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-The Court of Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the learned Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner/injured filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- along with interest @ 18% per annum for the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 28.11.2011.

It is stated by the petitioner that on 28.11.2011 at about 15.00 hours, when the petitioner/injured stood beside the Crane and when the said Crane Driver was lifting the iron pipes from the Truck in a rash and negligent manner, due to sudden jerk, all the pipes affixed to hook of the Crane fell down on the legs of the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner/injured sustained grievous bleeding injuries to his both legs and other injuries all over the body.
Based on a complaint, MGP,J the Station House Officer, Balanagar Police Station, registered a case in Crime No.497 of 2011 under Section 337 of IPC.

It is stated by the petitioner that he spent about Rs.2,00,000/- as inpatient towards treatment and his both legs were amputated and he cannot do his normal work and had to depend on attendant throughout his life and the Doctors have advised him for artificial limbs which may cost Rs.4,00,000/- and was also advised that the equipment has to be changed for every three years and due to the said accident, he became permanently disabled.

It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident, he was aged 19 years and was hale and healthy and used to earn Rs.5,000/- per month by working as 'Helper' and used to contribute the same towards his family.

Due to the ghastly accident, the petitioner has lost his entire income and suffered with pain and mental agony and hence claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- against the respondent Nos.1 & 2, who are the insurer and insured of the crime vehicle Crane bearing No.AP-28CB-9754.
4.
Respondent No.1, who is the Proprietor of the crime Crane bearing NoAP-28CB-9754, remained exparte.

5. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, occurrence of accident, age, earnings, occupation of the petitioner and denied that the vehicle was insured with the Insurance MGP,J Company and also contended that the 1st respondent has not reported regarding the alleged accident and hence, the Insurance Company is Lambadidaar Kailash Singh, Hyderabad vs M/S Bharat Crane And Heavy Machinery ... on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49236039/
1 not liable to pay compensation and that the compensation claimed is excess, exorbitant and hence prayed to dismiss the claim against it.

sentences.text:
6. Based on the above pleadings, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues for trial:-
i.

Whether the pleaded accident had occurred resulting in injuries to the petitioner,
Lambadidaar Kailash Singh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Crane bearing registration number AP-28-CB-9754) by its driver?
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation and if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of the respondents?

(iii) To what relief?
7.
Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioner/injured, PWs 1 to 5 were examined and Exs.A1 to A8 were marked.
On behalf of the 2nd respondent, no witness was examined however, Ex.B1-Copy of Insurance policy was marked.

8. Based on the evidence and documents available on record, the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition of the petitioner/injured by awarding compensation of Rs.12,64,000/-
along with simple interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by both the respondent MGP,J Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally.
Having not satisfied with the compensation awarded, the claim petitioner preferred the present Appeal seeking for enhancement of the same.

9. Heard learned counsel for the Appellant as well as learned Standing Counsel for Respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
10.

11. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel for the Respondent No.2/Insurance Company contended that the learned Tribunal, after considering all the aspects, had rightly awarded reasonable compensation and interference of this Court is unwarranted.
12.
Now, the point that emerges for consideration is, Whether the order of the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?

MGP,J POINT:-

2 13.
This Court has perused the entire evidence and documents available on record.
Petitioner/injured examined himself as PW1 and reiterated the contents made in the claim petition.
He deposed that due to the said accident, his both legs were amputated and he cannot do his normal work and had to depend on attendant throughout his life.
In support of his evidence, he filed Ex.A1-FIR registered by police of Balanagar, Ex

. A2-Charge sheet registered against the driver of the crime vehicle Crane, Ex.A3- Medico Legal Certificate which shows that the petitioner had sustained "Avulsion of right thigh medical aspect and Crush injury of both knee joints and legs,

Ex.A4- Discharge summary issued by BBR Multi speciality, Ex.A5- Final bills for a sum of Rs.1,23,867/-,
Ex.A6- Artificial limb estimation certificate, Ex.A7-Copy of Disability certificate and Ex.A8-Bunch of medical bills.

14. PW2, RMO of BBR Hospital, deposed in his evidence that the appellant took treatment in their Hospital for a period of one month three days and had not availed any insurance scheme or any other Government schemes.

PW3, Orthopaedic Surgeon of BBR Hospital, Hyderabad deposed in his evidence that the petitioner had underwent surgery for right above knee amputation and left knee disarticulation and again readmitted and operated for left stump and both his legs were amputated due to crush injuries MGP,J and he agreed with the disability assessed by the Gandhi Medical Board.

PW4, Associate Professor of Orthopaedics at Gandhi Hospital and also Member of Medical Board, deposed in his evidence that the percentage of disability sustained to the petitioner is 95%
which is permanent in nature and hence issued Ex.A7-Disability Certificate by following the guidelines of Mc.Bride Scale and Alimco Manual.
PW5, Regional Manager at Otto Bock deposed in his evidence that he examined the petitioner and issued estimation under Ex.A6 which requires socket replacement depending on the changes of the body.
15. Though PWs 1 to 5 were cross-examined at length, nothing worth was elicited from them to disbelieve their evidence.

Hence, from the evidence of PWs 1 to 5 coupled with the documents marked under Exs.A1 to A8, it is clearly established that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 28.11.2011 which resulted into amputation of his both legs.
16. The only aspect that has to be considered in the present Appeal is with regard to quantum of compensation.

A perusal of the compensation awarded shows that the learned Tribunal, after taking into consideration the occupation of the petitioner, in the absence of income proof, fixed the monthly income @ Rs.4,000/- and applied relevant multiplier and calculated compensation which arrived at Rs.8,64,000/-.

Apart from that, it also granted MGP,J Rs.1,00,000/- towards injury,
shock, pain and suffering, Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, extra nourishment, attendance,
transport and incidental charges and Rs.1,00,000/- towards artificial limbs which in total arrived at Rs.12,64,000/-.
17.
It is further contention of the learned counsel for appellant, that the learned Tribunal erred in considering the disability sustained by the petitioner.

As seen from the impugned order, the learned Tribunal while dealing with Issue no.1, had minutely discussed the disability aspect and stated that the permanent disability is economical as well as functional disability and will affect the earning capacity which may result in removal from his job.

Thus, considering the facts and circumstance of the case, it arrived at a conclusion that no further deduction is permissible and awarded an amount Lambadidaar Kailash Singh, Hyderabad vs M/S Bharat Crane And Heavy Machinery ... on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49236039/
3 of Rs.8,64,000/- towards loss of future earnings for which this Court considers it to be reasonable and sufficient.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, PW5- Orthotist of Otto Bock, stated in his cross-examination that after fixing artificial limbs, patient can walk with supportive devices i.e., stick/walker.
He also stated that Ex.A6 is only an estimation certificate and the appellant had not purchased any equipment from his Company.
18. Therefore, the learned Tribunal, considering the nature of injuries, disability sustained by the petitioner and all other aspects, had awarded reasonable amounts under different heads.
MGP,J Thus, this Court do not find any reason to interfere with the order passed by the learned Tribunal which is in proper perspective.
Hence, the Appeal is devoid of merits and substance and is liable to be dismissed.
19. In the result, the Appeal is dismissed without costs.
20. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
